memory_update.text: For the AI accelerators + HBM node, NVDA, MU, AMD, AVGO, and MRVL form the most direct US-listed candidate set for this pass: merchant GPUs, HBM memory, and custom XPU silicon.

HBM exposure is not only a memory-supplier issue; accelerator designers and custom silicon vendors are tightly exposed through platform qualification, HBM stack count, bandwidth, power, packaging yield, and hyperscaler deployment schedules.

Non-US primary HBM leaders SK hynix and Samsung Electronics are central to the chokepoint but were not included as candidates because this pass requested US-listed companies. They remain mandatory comparables for HBM share, pricing, and capacity evidence.

TSMC is a highly relevant ADR-listed advanced packaging and foundry chokepoint for AI accelerators and HBM integration, but was left outside the five-candidate limit to keep this pass focused on accelerator/HBM product leaders. It should be covered in a dedicated advanced packaging / foundry node pass.

Add MU as the most direct US-listed HBM supplier exposure for the AI accelerators and HBM memory node; prioritize HBM revenue, capacity sold-through, qualification status, and customer concentration in Layer 2.
Add AMAT and LRCX as HBM capacity-enabling wafer-fab/advanced-packaging equipment vendors; their relevance depends on incremental HBM process-step intensity and memory WFE order conversion.
Add KLAC and CAMT as yield-control and inspection/metrology plays for advanced packaging and HBM; CAMT is smaller but has unusually direct HBM/AI inspection order evidence.

For this node, the investable chokepoint map should separate direct HBM suppliers, HBM process-tool suppliers, advanced-packaging capacity, inspection/metrology yield tools, substrates/interposers, and accelerator customers.

Next pass should verify US-listed exposure to HBM substrates, interposers, thermal interface materials, test handlers/probers, EDA/IP for HBM PHY/controller integration, and OSAT/advanced-packaging providers with ADRs or US listings.
Add FORM as a high-priority HBM second-order candidate: probe-card demand is directly linked to HBM DRAM testing and generative-AI memory ramps.
Add TER as a high-priority HBM test candidate: Magnum 7H and annual-report language provide direct evidence of AI-driven HBM/DRAM memory-test exposure.
Add AMKR as an advanced-packaging/OSAT candidate: direct HBM packaging relevance is plausible, but revenue attribution to AI/HBM still needs stronger customer-level evidence.
Add CAMT as an inspection/metrology candidate for HBM, chiplets, memory, and advanced packaging; evidence is company-disclosed but revenue segmentation needs verification.
Add ONTO as a process-control/metrology candidate for HBM/GPU AI packages; direct tool relevance is clear, but customer qualification evidence should be checked.
For the AI accelerators + HBM node, include test, probe-card, metrology, and advanced-packaging suppliers as first-class chokepoint-adjacent mappings, not only GPU, memory, and foundry names.

Need a follow-up pass on materials and consumables for HBM/advanced packaging, including temporary bonding, electroplating chemistry, substrates/interposers, thermal interface materials, and ultra-clean process inputs.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Focused Layer 1B expansion for the AI accelerators + HBM memory node identified five US-listed companies with the most direct public-market exposure: NVIDIA and AMD as merchant AI accelerator platforms, Micron as the direct US-listed HBM memory supplier, and Broadcom and Marvell as custom AI accelerator / XPU silicon platforms. The node appears structurally important because modern AI accelerators bind together compute dies, HBM stacks, advanced packaging, networking I/O, and hyperscaler qualification cycles. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded the US-listed universe around the HBM/AI-accelerator chokepoint into memory supply, wafer-fab equipment, advanced-packaging tools, inspection/metrology, and process-control yield nodes. The highest-relevance additions for this pass are MU, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC, and CAMT; all appear to clear the USD 1B market-cap preference based on current market data, but this is not a recommendation and requires deeper evidence checks on revenue exposure, customer concentration, and cycle risk. Expanded the US-listed universe around the AI accelerator + HBM node toward less obvious second-order chokepoint exposures. The most relevant additions are not only GPU/ASIC and memory vendors, but also wafer probe cards, HBM memory testers, advanced packaging/test capacity, and inspection/metrology suppliers needed to raise HBM and 2.5D/3D package yields. All five candidates screened above USD 1B market cap using current web finance data, but inclusion is research-priority only, not a trading recommendation.
